source_text: (Sed Christus diuortium inhibet dicens: qui dimiserit uxorem suam et aliam duxerit, adulterium committet, (et) qui dimissam a uiro duxerit, aeque adulter est, - ut sic quoque prohibeat diuortium, inlicitum facit repudiatae matrimonium — Moyses uero permittit repudium in Deuteronomio: si sumserit quis uxorem et habitauerit cum ea, et euenerit non inuenire eam apud eum gratiam, eo quod inuentum sit in illa impudicum negotium, scribet libellum repudii et dabit in manu eius et dimittet illam de domo sua.
pass_a_gloss: But Christ forbids divorce, saying: he who dismisses his wife and leads another, commits adultery, and he who leads her who has been dismissed by her husband, is equally an adulterer, - so that He also forbids divorce, makes the marriage of her who has been repudiated unlawful — But Moses permits repudiation in Deuteronomy: if someone takes a wife and dwells with her, and it happens that he does not find her favor with him, because an impudent deed is found in her, he will write a bill of repudiation and give it into her hand and dismiss her from his house.

pass_b_english: Christ forbids divorce, saying that anyone who dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery, and that anyone who marries a woman dismissed by her husband is equally an adulterer—so that He also forbids divorce by making the marriage of a repudiated woman unlawful. Moses, however, permits repudiation in Deuteronomy: if a man takes a wife, lives with her, and then finds no favor in her because he discovers an indecent deed in her, he is to write a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her out of his house (Deuteronomy).

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The scripture reference (Deuteronomy) is correctly identified as the source of the Moses passage. The title 'Christ Teaches Against Divorce' correctly names the thought.
